content: This SRS specifies the functional and non-functional requirements for a web application designed to encrypt and decrypt images. The application aims to provide users with a secure way to store and share sensitive images.

 Fonts: Standard fonts are used throughout the document.
 Bold: May be used to emphasize key terms or requirements.
 Italics: May be used to reference figures or tables within the document.
 Priorities: Every requirement statement will have its own assigned priority (e.g., High, Medium, Low) for clarity.

This SRS is intended for various audiences:
 Developers: Responsible for implementing the functionalities outlined in the document.
 Project Managers: Overseeing the development process and ensuring adherence to requirements.
 Testers: Designing and executing test cases to verify application functionality.
 Users: Gaining an understanding of the application's capabilities and limitations.
The document is structured as follows:
 Introduction (This section)
 Overall Description (Describes the application's general features)
 Specific Requirements (Detailed functional and non-functional requirements)
 System Interfaces (Defines how the application interacts with external systems)
 Other Non-Functional Requirements (Security, performance, etc.)
 Appendix (Includes additional information such as data models or error messages)
We recommend readers begin with the Introduction and Overall Description, followed by sections most relevant to their role in the project.

This SRS focuses on the core functionalities of the image encryption application:
 Users can select images from their device storage.
 The application encrypts chosen images using a user-defined password or key.
 Encrypted images are stored within the application in a secure format.
 Users can decrypt previously encrypted images using the same password or key.
 Encrypted images should be unreadable by unauthorized user

This section will be filled with specific references during the SRS development process, potentially including:
 Security standards for data encryption (e.g., AES-256)
 User interface style guides for web applications

This image encryption application is a new, self-contained web application designed to be accessed through a standard web browser. Users will interact with the application entirely through the web interface.

 Image Selection: Users can browse and select images from their local device storage for upload and encryption.
 Encryption: The application encrypts uploaded images using a user-defined password or key on the server-side. Encrypted data is never stored unencrypted on the user's device.
 Secure Storage: Encrypted images are stored securely on the application's server using industry-standard encryption methods.
 Decryption: Users can decrypt previously uploaded and encrypted images using the same password or key, retrieving them for viewing or downloading.
 Image Management: The web application allows users to view, organize, potentially delete, and download encrypted images stored on the server.

 Primary Users: Individuals who prioritize securing their sensitive images through a web interface accessible from any device with a web browser. They may have a basic understanding of encryption concepts but are not necessarily technical experts.
 Secondary Users: Users who occasionally need to encrypt images for specific purposes using a web interface. They may require a clear and user-friendly interface with minimal technical knowledge required.

 Hardware Platform: The application is web-based and accessible from any device with a standard web browser and internet connection.
 Operating System: The application should be compatible with major operating systems (Windows, macOS, Linux) through their respective web browsers.
 Other Software: The application should coexist peacefully with user's web browser and internet connection.

 Security: The primary constraint remains robust encryption using industry-standard algorithms (e.g., AES-256) on the server-side. User passwords should be securely stored using hashing and salting techniques. Data transmission between user and server should be encrypted using HTTPS protocol.
 Performance: The application should be optimized for efficient image upload, encryption, decryption, and download processes, minimizing server load and user wait times.
 Usability: The web interface should be intuitive and user-friendly, catering to users with varying technical expertise.
 Browser Compatibility: The application should function consistently across major web browsers (e.g., Chrome, Firefox, Safari) with minimal browser-specific adjustments.

The following user documentation components will be delivered alongside the image encryption web application:
User Manual: A comprehensive user manual in a downloadable PDF format will be provided. It will detail the application's functionalities, step-by-step instructions for image encryption, decryption, management, and troubleshooting tips.
Online Help: Contextual help will be integrated within the web application interface. Users can access brief explanations and instructions by hovering over specific features or clicking on designated help buttons.
Tutorials: A series of short video tutorials will be available on the application's website or a designated video platform. These tutorials will visually demonstrate key functionalities for users who prefer a video-based learning approach.

The following assumptions and dependencies are made for the image encryption web application:
Users have a basic understanding of web browsing and file management on their devices.
Users have a reliable internet connection for uploading and downloading images.
The web application server has sufficient processing power and storage capacity to handle encryption and decryption processes.
The web application server is configured with a secure web server certificate (HTTPS) for encrypted data transmission.

The web application will have a user-friendly and intuitive interface accessible through standard web browsers.
A consistent visual design will be maintained throughout the application.
The UI will follow industry best practices for web application design, ensuring clarity and ease of use.
Standard navigation elements (menus, buttons) will be used for consistent user experience.
Contextual help will be available through tooltips or dedicated help buttons for each functionality.
Error messages will be clear, concise, and actionable, guiding users towards resolving issues.
A detailed user interface design document will be created separately, outlining specific screen layouts, element functionalities, and visual style.
This web application is browser-based and doesn't require specific hardware interaction beyond a standard internet connection.>

The application will interact with a secure server-side database to store encrypted images and user information.
The database schema will be defined to ensure data integrity and security.
The application will utilize a server-side scripting language (e.g., Python, Node.js) to handle image encryption and decryption processes.
Secure communication protocols (HTTPS) will be used for all data transmission between user and server.
An API (Application Programming Interface) may be developed to allow for potential future integrations with other applications (TBD).

The application will rely on a stable internet connection for users to upload images, interact with the web interface, and download encrypted data.
Data transfer between user and server will be encrypted using HTTPS protocol to ensure data privacy.
Standard web communication protocols (HTTP) will be used for communication between user browser and the server.

This feature allows users to select images from their local device storage for upload and subsequent encryption. (High Priority)
User navigates to the "Upload Images" section of the application.
User clicks the "Browse Files" button or utilizes a drag-and-drop functionality to select images.
The application displays a preview of the selected images.
User confirms image selection for upload.
REQ-1: The application shall allow users to select multiple images for upload in a single session.
REQ-2: The application shall display clear file size limitations for supported image formats (e.g., JPEG, PNG).
REQ-3: The application shall provide a visual preview of selected images before upload.
REQ-4: The application shall offer basic image editing options (e.g., rotate, crop) before upload (TBD).
REQ-5: The application shall display a progress indicator during image upload.
REQ-6: Upon successful upload, the application shall confirm the number of uploaded images and provide options for encryption.

This feature allows users to encrypt uploaded images using a user-defined password or key. (High Priority)
User selects an uploaded image for encryption.
User enters a desired password or key for encryption.
User confirms encryption request.
REQ-7: The application shall utilize a robust and industry-standard encryption algorithm (e.g., AES-256) for image encryption.
REQ-8: The application shall encrypt images on the server-side, never storing unencrypted images on the user's device.
REQ-9: The application shall offer password strength indicators to guide users in creating secure passwords.
REQ-10: The application shall allow users to re-enter passwords for confirmation to minimize typos.
REQ-11: The application shall not store user passwords in plain text. Secure hashing and salting techniques must be used. (TBD)
REQ-12: The application shall display a confirmation message upon successful image encryption.

Image Upload and Download: Image upload and download times should be optimized for efficient user experience. The application should strive for a maximum wait time of 10 seconds for uploads and downloads of images under 5MB in size on a stable internet connection. (Target)
Encryption and Decryption: Encryption and decryption processes should be completed within a reasonable timeframe based on image size. Users should not experience delays exceeding 15 seconds for encrypting or decrypting images under 5MB. (Target)
Server Response: The application should maintain a responsive user interface with minimal lag between user actions and system responses. (Target)
These performance targets may be adjusted based on further testing and resource allocation during development.
This web application does not pose any physical safety hazards during its operation.

Data Security: Encrypted images and user passwords must be stored securely on the server using industry-standard encryption methods (e.g., AES-256). (High Priority)
Data Transmission: All communication between user and server, including image uploads, downloads, and password transmission, must be encrypted using HTTPS protocol. (High Priority)
User Authentication: Users must be authenticated through a secure login process to access uploaded and encrypted images. Password complexity requirements should be enforced. (High Priority)
Session Management: User sessions should have a timeout mechanism for automatic logout after a period of inactivity to prevent unauthorized access. (Medium Priority)
Regular Security Audits: The application and server infrastructure should undergo regular security audits to identify and address potential vulnerabilities. (Medium Priority)

Usability: The user interface should be intuitive and user-friendly, catering to users with varying technical expertise. Clear instructions and tooltips should be provided for each functionality. (High Priority)
Reliability: The application should function reliably with minimal downtime or errors. (High Priority)
Maintainability: The application code should be well-structured, documented, and modular for ease of maintenance and future updates. (Medium Priority)
Scalability: The application should be designed to accommodate a growing user base and potential future feature additions. (Medium Priority)

User accounts are required for accessing uploaded and encrypted images.
Users are responsible for maintaining the security of their passwords.
The application will not be liable for any loss of data due to user negligence or forgotten passwords.
Internationalization: The application interface should be designed to support potential future localization for different languages. (Low Priority)
